learning_outcomes.text: Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Basic knowledge about the use and programming of computers, operating systems, databases, and computer programs with application in engineering.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, enabling them to learn new methods and theories, and providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Propose creative solutions to satisfactorily respond to real needs and problems of society.
Effectively apply techniques related to bibliographic search and the use of reliable data sources or other information systems.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to the environment and characteristics of the C language.
Structure and elements of a program.
Use of pointers for passing variables between functions.
Character strings. Functions on character strings.
teaching_methods: Presentation of contents by the teaching staff (Theoretical Class)
Group work sessions supervised by the teaching staff (Practical Classes)
Activities carried out in spaces with specialized equipment (Laboratory)
Realization and exhibition of a work related to the subject (Teamwork)
Realization of a project to solve a problem or address a task by planning, designing and carrying out a series of activities (Teamwork / Integrated Project)
Personalized attention and in small group (Tutorship)
Individual and group preparation of essays, problem solving, projects, etc. (Team Work)
assessment_rules: The 1st call assessment combines on-site lab practices (10%), non face-to-face practices (30%), a final exam (35% with a minimum of 4/10), and an integrated project (25%). To pass, a total grade of 5/10 is required. For the 2nd call, students can retain previous marks for practices and project, or retake them; a multiple-choice exam (35% or 50%) is taken, requiring a minimum of 4/10, optionally with a computer-based practical exam (40% or 50%). AI tool usage is regulated across three levels, from not permitted (Level 1) to permitted with full traceability (Level 3), with unpermitted or uncited use considered academic misconduct.
